title: Password Strength Checker
story: Every website demands a 'strong password' but nobody explains what that means. You decide to write your own strength checker — length check, uppercase check, and a final verdict, all powered by Boolean logic.
why: Boolean-returning functions can be combined with logical operators to build sophisticated multi-condition checkers from simple building blocks.
analogy: Password checking is like airport security with multiple screening stations. Station 1 checks ID length, Station 2 checks for special features (uppercase). Your `is_strong` function is the final security officer who says 'yes' only if ALL stations gave a thumbs-up.
try_it: Add a third check function called `has_digit(pw: Str) -> Bool` and include it in `is_strong`. Test with passwords like "NoDigits" and "Has1Digit".
tips: Build small Boolean checkers first, then combine them with && or ||
Use string.str_lower to detect uppercase: if lowering changes the string, uppercase existed
is_strong acts as a 'summary' function that delegates to the individual checkers
Test each checker independently before combining them
common_mistakes: Confusing the logic: `string.str_upper(pw) != pw` detects LOWERCASE, not uppercase
Forgetting to import or use string functions with the `string.` prefix
Using `||` when you need `&&` — all conditions must pass for a strong password
